# Tic-Tac-Toe: Proposed Canon Draft r2

Status: in-progress; readiness: not-assessed. Current draft owner: ADHOC-7fd789738d5348cbbbd4f4cb378fbecf, workflow.planning, request tic-tac-toe-canon-r2. This is an explicit reconciliation of retained draft tic-tac-toe-canon-r1, not admission or a complete proposal. r2 is the current draft; r1 remains its immutable predecessor. The current candidate set is the retained r1 candidates listed below plus the specified revisions/additions. No candidate is silently dropped. Read this amendment with the full retained r1 in the same capture, not as a second plan.

## Exact Inputs And Coverage

Input capture SHA-256 d96c7dfa21082401fb0845ea96f9ba6d82b890fc8b37474316adfc3cd3b7838e. Predecessor request file SHA-256 7ac28f9bf3aca134f6f52fb082868610db59a3bb17bdbe3b4e90603522e430c4. All four selected sources were inventoried and semantically considered; no source was omitted or only counted.
- source-1, original game intent and clarification: d6139844ec225d1e36ddd07d9552bc8aa1a64fc14a38fc6b935560f49bea69ed.
- source-2, manual replay decision: 7af814bf2cd85e7440edec3184c9e505435e77ebf8d7fad2359c3b2ed884e961.
- source-3, Express/port/browser requirements: 3546cbb855ed4253554279579fe77387fb3eaccfe03310fe79b5f2db2e44e616.
- source-4, four confirmed defaults and authority to append/reconcile: 677069c28c0a4c38ba1772b07b82c664fd8c82a29f1465615b8488424e9f90b8.

source-4 records the actual 'Yes' to the four recommendations and 'run both' to the two named operations. It is not approval of all of r1. Source precedence is limited to explicit decisions: source-2 resolves automatic-repeat ambiguity, source-3 requires Express despite an earlier browser-only suggestion, and source-4 settles the four defaults below. Earlier source bytes remain unchanged. The unrelated checklist sample, PokerNight pack and historical horizon are excluded. No diagram inputs, operational base or execution snapshot are added by this revision.

## Retained Candidates

Retain verbatim meaning, revision and provenance from r1 for definitions d-human-count@r1, d-ai@r1, d-game@r1 and d-replay@r1; and requirements r-rules@r1, r-mark-choice@r1, r-unbeatable@r1, r-result@r1, r-react@r1 and r-runtime@r1. Their full content remains in tic-tac-toe-canon-r1. Definition authority stays proposed product vocabulary in this capture, not admitted glossary authority; aliases and exclusions remain as recorded.

In particular, retain standard 3x3 rules, X-first alternating turns, occupied-cell rejection, all eight winning lines, win-before-draw precedence and no terminal moves. Retain human X/O choice, React, Express on local port 3630, clear turn/results, and AI that cannot lose as either mark from a fresh legal game. Two unbeatable AIs draw. Retain exhaustive legal-opponent-sequence testing and coverage of every permitted AI tie-break choice; a handful of successful sample games is insufficient. These summaries do not narrow the retained acceptance criteria.

## Revised And Added Requirements

- r-modes@r2 (requirement; revise r-modes@r1; sources 1 and 4): support 0 humans (AI/AI), 1 human (human/AI) and 2 humans (human/human) within one shared-device game. In two-human mode, both people take turns using the same browser/device; there is no cross-device multiplayer. A phone loading the application accesses its own game, not a synchronized second player in a desktop game. Human input cannot place moves on AI-controlled turns. Acceptance: complete a game in each mode; zero-human play advances without board input, two-human play has no autonomous moves, and controller ownership follows the mode. Uses d-human-count@r1, r-rules@r1 and r-local-session@r1. The original source-1 scope is retained; shared-device intent is now confirmed by source-4.

- r-manual-replay@r2 (requirement; revise r-manual-replay@r1; sources 2 and 4): in every mode, the finished board/result remains visible until a person activates 'Play again' or deliberately selects another permitted setup action. No mode automatically repeats. 'Play again' clears the board and terminal result, retains the selected mode and human mark, and starts one new game with X first. No move or callback from the previous game may affect the new game. Acceptance: exercise replay after wins and draws in human modes and after the AI/AI draw; verify no repeat while waiting, retained selections and correct first controller. For a human choosing O, the AI opens as X after the delay in r-ai-pacing@r1. Uses d-replay@r1, r-rules@r1 and r-modes@r2. Deliberate setup changes outside Play again remain governed by the unresolved setup recommendation, not an automatic reset exception.

- r-browsers@r2 (requirement; revise r-browsers@r1; sources 3 and 4): retain responsive desktop/mobile browser behavior and usable pointer/touch controls. Validation must include a physical phone accessing the local Express server over Wi-Fi, not mobile emulation alone. The server's accessible local-network address uses port 3630; the phone's localhost is not the desktop server. Acceptance: load the actual React application and complete/replay games on the selected desktop and physical-phone browsers; verify the full board, mode/mark controls and result are accessible without overlap or clipping and touchscreen actions work correctly. Record actual devices, browser versions, viewport and access URL in implementation evidence. Choosing a bind address and any local firewall setup is implementation/setup work; this requirement does not authorize public exposure. Uses r-runtime@r1 and r-modes@r2. The earlier proposed exact browser/version matrix is not implicitly approved.

- r-local-session@r1 (requirement; add; source-4): provide one shared-device game with no accounts, saved games or persistent scores. No account setup or login is required to play. Acceptance: launch directly into the game/setup flow without account creation and verify there is no saved-game or persistent-score feature. The no-persistence scope does not prohibit transient state needed for the current game or mode/mark retention on Play again. Do not infer a scoreboard from the word 'scores'; none is requested. This settles the relevant part of a-session from draft r1.

- r-ai-pacing@r1 (requirement; add; source-4): schedule each AI move with a 500 ms delay before applying it, including an opening AI move and every AI/AI turn. This is a pacing delay, not a hard real-time deadline; browsers may delay callbacks in background tabs or under load. Acceptance: controlled-clock tests show no move before the delay and one legal move when the scheduled turn runs; foreground browser observation shows distinct moves. AI moves occur only in the current active game's AI-controlled turn, never after a terminal result or from a stale prior game. No multiple-move jump from stacked callbacks is allowed. Uses r-rules@r1, r-modes@r2 and r-manual-replay@r2. This makes a-pacing from r1 a settled requirement.

## Updated Story Traceability

Keep all four local story identities; revise each to r2 for its updated relationships and confirmed scope.
- s-solo@r2 (story; sources 1 and 4): a human chooses X or O and plays against an unbeatable AI, then can replay with the same settings. Satisfied by r-rules@r1, r-modes@r2, r-mark-choice@r1, r-unbeatable@r1, r-result@r1, r-manual-replay@r2 and r-ai-pacing@r1.
- s-watch@r2 (story; sources 1, 2 and 4): an observer watches two unbeatable AIs play with 500 ms turn pacing, sees the draw and initiates another game with Play again. Satisfied by r-modes@r2, r-unbeatable@r1, r-result@r1, r-manual-replay@r2 and r-ai-pacing@r1.
- s-two-humans@r2 (story; sources 1 and 4): two people share one device, alternate legal moves, see the result and choose replay. Satisfied by r-rules@r1, r-modes@r2, r-result@r1, r-manual-replay@r2 and r-local-session@r1.
- s-local-browser@r2 (story; sources 1, 3 and 4): a user plays the React game served locally by Express on port 3630 in a desktop browser or physical-phone browser on local Wi-Fi. Satisfied by r-react@r1, r-runtime@r1, r-browsers@r2 and r-local-session@r1.

## Disposition Of Prior Assumptions

- a-session: shared-device game, no accounts, saved games or persistent scores are settled by source-4 and r-local-session@r1. Browser refresh returning to setup, absence of transient scores, database choice and internal state placement were not individually approved. No networked multiplayer, additional difficulty levels or external AI service is requested; these remain outside the selected simple scope, not selected implementation technologies.
- a-replay: manual replay in every mode with mode/mark retention is settled by source-4 and r-manual-replay@r2. The recommendation to permit setup changes only before a game's first move or after termination remains unconfirmed. No newly imposed restriction is hidden inside the confirmation.
- a-pacing: settled as r-ai-pacing@r1. The interpretation as scheduled delay rather than exact wall-clock execution is an engineering clarification of browser behavior.
- a-compatibility: desktop/mobile testing with a real phone is settled. The proposed Chrome/Firefox/Safari, iOS/Android and 1280x800/390x844/320px-width matrix plus keyboard/focus recommendations remain proposed engineering acceptance details, not confirmed statements by the Operator.
- a-connectivity: physical-phone access to the local server over Wi-Fi is settled. Exact LAN bind address, firewall steps and browser/device selection remain implementation/setup decisions; no public hosting or network configuration is performed during planning.

## Tradeoffs, Risks And Impact

Manual replay preserves the result for inspection and avoids an endless AI demonstration. Retaining mode/mark selections avoids repetitive setup. The 500 ms delay makes AI turns observable while retaining unbeatable move selection; computation strategy is not dictated. No accounts or durable game storage keeps this bounded. Actual-phone validation addresses a gap that viewport emulation cannot cover.

Reconcile future work and tests for all-mode replay, timer cancellation, fixed-port serving, touch input and LAN access. Exhaustive AI verification and stale-callback risks from r1 remain. A phone requirement does not mean remote humans share a board. LAN serving introduces a network-access consideration; deliberate local binding and no assumed public exposure mitigate it. No runtime behavior or implementation has been validated by these planning checks.

This changes candidate acceptance obligations and relationships only. There are no complete proposals, work drafts, phase files, admitted records, execution statuses or DAG edges to update in this capture. No completed phase is reopened and no historical compliance finding is asserted. No existing independent review or approval is carried forward; r1 remains historical rather than approved for the expanded four-source subject. Operational base and execution snapshot were absent at r1 inspection and none has been supplied by this confirmation. Resolve the exact target/baseline before a complete proposal; do not infer that the tic-tac-toe test belongs in PokerNight product Canon.

## Representation And Next Step

Only existing definition, requirement and story kinds are used. Semantic relationships, acceptance examples, candidate revisions and assumption dispositions stay in text; no schema expansion is requested. Prior request files, capture snapshots and source bytes are retained. The current set has four retained definitions, eleven requirements (six retained, three revised, two added) and four revised stories.

Next is separately authorized work shaping against this current candidate set. Carry the remaining engineering recommendations explicitly and settle affected acceptance/setup choices before claiming a complete proposal. No source scrub, formal review, approval, admission, product implementation, server launch or forge operation is authorized by this reconciliation.
questions: Resolve the setup-change behavior before completing the interaction contract; r1 recommended changing mode/mark only before the first move or after termination, but this was not one of the four confirmed defaults.

Select and document the exact desktop/physical-phone browser/version and viewport validation matrix during work shaping; physical-phone testing over local Wi-Fi is already confirmed and must not be replaced by emulation alone.
Before complete proposal/admission, select the intended destination and exact operational baseline/execution snapshot without silently treating this test feature as PokerNight product scope.
